P8p: When you create a rule to deal with a collision of two principles, store the hard case along with it: what happened, the principles that actually conflicted, your first judgments, your final decision and rationale, any dissenting opinions, the consequences, and which version of the rule it was decided under. When the rule changes, run the case through again. That saves each generation from having to rediscover the same constitutional fight from scratch.
P8t: When you create a rule to deal with a collision of two principles, don't only store the rule. Any dissenting opinions should go in there as well, along with the consequences and which version of the rule it was decided under. When the rule changes, run the case through again. That saves each generation from having to rediscover the same constitutional fight from scratch.
